entries.description: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. entries.title: On the hunt for dark matter
entries.description: From Broadway to MIT’s Laboratory for Nuclear Science, PhD student Jessica Fry doesn’t do anything halfway. Now she’s hunting for the universe’s most elusive particle.

entries.description: When Dehn Gilmore, professor of English at Caltech, was investigating ideas for her next book, she had to look no further than her own family tree. entries.title: How a medical database developed at MIT evolved into a global standard of data-sharing
entries.description: The visionary PhysioNet platform launched 25 years ago, based on a system developed at MIT in the 1970s. It has become one of the most comprehensive biomedical and clinical data repositories in existence.

entries.title: MIT and Broad Institute researchers break diffraction barrier in super-resolution microscopy
entries.description: New U-STORM imaging technology lets scientists view molecular structures in subatomic detail — about 1,000 times clearer than traditional dyes — while making the microscope process much simpler.

entries.title: Yu Deng ’11 and Hong Wang PhD ’19 awarded Fields Medal
entries.description: MIT-trained mathematicians earn the honor, one of the most prestigious in the field, for their significant achievements.

entries.title: JWST finds early galaxies may be 4 times more massive than thought
entries.description: Astronomers using JWST have discovered that massive early galaxies contain far more small, faint stars than expected. That hidden population could make some of these galaxies three to four times more massive than previous estimates. The finding makes it even harder to explain how enormous, mature galaxies formed so soon after the Big Bang. It could also suggest that planets around low-mass stars were more common in the early universe than scientists realized.

entries.title: Hidden magnetism inside atoms may explain mysterious gamma rays
entries.description: For decades, scientists have puzzled over why certain atomic nuclei unexpectedly produce large numbers of low-energy gamma rays. A new experiment traced the effect to magnetic changes inside the nucleus, where protons and neutrons effectively flip their tiny internal magnets. The discovery could sharpen models of everything from nuclear reactions on Earth to the creation of heavy elements in stars and neutron star mergers.

entries.title: A 0.42-nanometer breakthrough could push transistors beyond silicon
entries.description: Atomically thin semiconductors could enable dramatically smaller and more efficient chips, but a stubborn problem at the boundary between materials has limited their performance. Researchers have now engineered that atomic interface to protect electron flow while still allowing extremely thin insulating layers. The resulting transistors delivered an unusually strong combination of electrical control and performance.

entries.title: Youth advocates gather in New York to launch new AI standards
entries.description: As artificial intelligence (AI) rapidly transforms everything from how we learn, to the job market, children are adopting the technology more than three times faster than adults – exposing them to unique opportunities and risks.

entries.title: Mount Olympus and D-Day beaches among new World Heritage Sites
entries.description: From the peaks of Mount Olympus in Greece to the shores of the “D-Day” beaches in France, 25 cultural or natural landmarks from across the globe have been newly inscribed on the World Heritage List, updated annually by the UN Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO).

entries.title: UN calls for urgent action to protect children from online information risks
entries.description: More than eight in 10 young people aged 15 to 24 worldwide are now online, and in low-income countries they outpace the rest of the population nearly two to one.

entries.title: ADB Approves Project to Expand Access to Life-Saving Care in Mongolia’s Provinces
entries.description: ADB has approved a $225 million loan—its largest health sector investment in Mongolia—to expand access to quality health care across the country’s provinces through major upgrades in health infrastructure, emergency care, digital health systems, medical equipment, and workforce capacity.

entries.title: ADB Approves $1 Billion Loan to Support Sustainable Growth and Resilience of India’s Cities
entries.description: ADB has approved a $1 billion loan to support the Government of India’s urban reform agenda by maintaining momentum of investment and reforms aimed at transforming cities into engines of economic growth, innovation, and livability.

entries.title: ADB, FSM Development Bank to Support Women Entrepreneurs in the Federated States of Micronesia
entries.description: ADB has signed a $5 million financing package with Federated States of Micronesia Development Bank (FSMDB) to expand access to finance for women-led small and medium-sized enterprises in the Federated States of Micronesia.

entries.title: ADB to Deploy $450 Million to Shield Cambodia, Sri Lanka from Middle East Impact
entries.description: ADB is set to deploy $450 million to protect poor households and strengthen the economies of Cambodia and Sri Lanka as the conflict in the Middle East drives up costs and deepens uncertainty across Asia and the Pacific.

entries.title: ADB Supports Tbilisi Bypass with $250 Million Loan to Boost Georgia’s Regional Connectivity
entries.description: ADB has approved a $250 million loan to help build a critical bypass around Tbilisi that will improve road connectivity, ease congestion, and strengthen Georgia’s role as a regional transport hub in the region.

entries.title: ADB Approves $850 Million Loan to Accelerate Affordable Rooftop Solar Adoption for Households in India
entries.description: ADB has approved an $850 million loan to support reforms that will speed up the rollout of the Government of India’s flagship rooftop solar program, boosting the resilience of Indian households through better access to affordable clean energy, mobilizing private sector investment, and strengthening the skills of grid personnel and rural entrepreneurs.

entries.title: ADB, Japan Establish New Water Security Fund
entries.description: ADB and the Government of Japan established a new fund to strengthen water security and protect people across Asia and the Pacific from worsening floods, droughts, and other water-related shocks. Japan will make an initial $10 million contribution to the fund.

entries.title: ADB Sells $2 Billion 10-Year Global Benchmark Bond
entries.description: ADB has priced a $2 billion 10-year global bond, proceeds of which will become part of ADB’s ordinary capital resources.

entries.title: ADB Puts Team on the Ground in Türkiye as Financing Demand Surges
entries.description: Recognizing Türkiye’s growing regional importance, the Asian Development Bank (ADB) will establish an office in the country as it prepares to commit about $3 billion a year to earthquake recovery, critical infrastructure, businesses, and trade routes linking Asia and Europe.

entries.title: ADB Provides $2 Million Grant to Support Flood-Affected Communities in Thailand
entries.description: ADB has approved a $2 million grant to support the Government of Thailand as it expands humanitarian assistance for communities devastated by severe flooding in southern Thailand.

entries.title: After post-pandemic improvement, youth unemployment is rising again
entries.description: Frustrated by skyrocketing youth unemployment, among other issues, tens of thousands of Gen Z activists took to the streets of Nepal last year, demanding a stake in the country’s economic growth. The protest worked and the prime minister resigned.

entries.title: Global hunger declines again but progress remains uneven across regions
entries.description: Global hunger declined for a third consecutive year in 2025 showing that progress is possible, but gains remain fragile and far too slow to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by the 2030 deadline.

entries.title: ADB Loan Supports Stronger Earthquake Resilience at Schools in Armenia
entries.description: ADB and the Government of Armenia have signed a $293 million loan agreement to expand resilient, inclusive school infrastructure nationwide and strengthen the country's capacity to manage earthquake risks.

entries.title: Multilateral Development Banks Increase Climate Finance to Record $163 Billion in 2025, Supporting Resilient and Sustainable Growth
entries.description: MDBs increased climate finance to record levels in 2025, reinforcing their role in supporting resilient and sustainable economies.

entries.title: As aid dries up, countries pledge to close the $4 trillion development gap
entries.description: UN Member States reaffirmed their commitment to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by adopting a declaration on Wednesday that they will implement reforms to help close the $4 trillion SDG financing gap.

entries.title: World News in Brief: Gaza aid challenges persist, renewed push for clean energy, Sudan cholera update
entries.description: Humanitarians in the Gaza Strip continue to face significant challenges in reaching communities located near the so-called “Yellow Line” in northern Rafah, the UN aid coordination office OCHA said on Tuesday.

entries.title: Despite hurdles, don’t give up on Sustainable Development Goals, UN urges
entries.description: In a world of “parallel realities” where stark inequalities seemingly divide people and challenge the promise of multilateralism, the vision of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) is to bring people together and help them achieve a better reality.

entries.title: ADB President Urges Faster Action on Water Security
entries.description: ADB President Masato Kanda has called for faster investment and reform to secure water across Asia and the Pacific, pointing to a new ADB-administered fund with Japan that will help developing economies strengthen disaster preparedness, infrastructure, and water management.

entries.title: ADB Launches Initiative to Bring Japanese Startup Innovation to Southeast Asia and the Pacific
entries.description: ADB and the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) have launched the Southeast Asia Emerging Entrepreneurs Kickstart initiative to help promising startups scale solutions to complex development challenges in Southeast Asia and the Pacific.

entries.title: New initiative launched to shield terrorism victims from online harm
entries.description: The UN has launched a new initiative to protect victims of terrorist attacks from online harm and re-traumatisation, drawing on harrowing survivor accounts, from the Nova Music Festival in Israel to an attack on a FIFA World Cup final viewing party in Uganda.

entries.title: 75 years later, the promise to protect refugees faces its greatest test
entries.description: As the world marks the 75th anniversary of the Refugee Convention, the UN refugee agency (UNHCR) has launched a global campaign urging governments, organizations and individuals to renew their commitment to protecting people forced to flee war, violence and persecution.

entries.title: UN chief hails Syria’s ‘moment of possibility’ on first visit since fall of Assad regime
entries.description: Syria has an opportunity not only to recover from conflict but to build “a future that is more stable, more inclusive and more prosperous for all Syrians”, UN Secretary-General António Guterres said in Damascus on Saturday as he began a landmark visit to the country.

entries.title: Security Council LIVE: Drone strikes and political impasse in Libya
entries.description: As Libya faces a political impasse delaying long-planned elections alongside clashes and drone strikes that left a major oil refinery ablaze, the Security Council heard the latest updates, with an activist warning that the collision of extreme heat, water scarcity and environmental shocks with political division, armed insecurity and struggling institutions clearly makes the situation a peace and security issue. UN News app users can follow our live coverage here.

entries.title: Gaza: Destruction of buildings rises by nearly 10 per cent since ceasefire
entries.description: New satellite assessments show the destruction of buildings in Gaza has climbed by nearly 10 per cent since October’s faltering ceasefire between Hamas and Israeli forces aim to end the two-year war, which reduced cities to rubble and displaced more than one million people, UN agencies said on Thursday.

entries.title: Lebanon: UN peacekeepers count hundreds of Israeli strikes and incursions in a single weekend
entries.description: Israeli forces fired 455 projectiles into south Lebanon and breached Lebanese airspace 97 times between Friday and Sunday, the UN's peacekeeping mission in the country reported Monday – among the heaviest fire seen in months.

entries.title: Fighting deepens needs and fuels further displacement in Sudan
entries.description: Ongoing conflict, displacement and funding shortages continue to deepen needs in Sudan, the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) warned on Monday, underscoring the need for greater civilian protection.

entries.title: Security Council LIVE: Warnings of famine and collapse as South Sudan's peace deal frays
entries.description: Nearly eight million people in South Sudan – more than half the population – face crisis-level hunger, with famine risk now flagged in four counties, as the Security Council met this morning in New York. A cholera outbreak has killed more than 1,700 people, and some aid workers are being killed and abducted even as they try to reach those most at risk. Follow live coverage below.

entries.title: Security Council LIVE: International Criminal Court briefs on Darfur
entries.description: On Wednesday, the Security Council heard an update on the International Criminal Court's work in Sudan's Darfur region, referred to the Court back in 2005. Focus has recently turned to atrocities in the ongoing war between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF). The briefing was held as the ICC faces mounting pressure: this week, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio launched a campaign to “dismantle” the Court, which prosecutes individuals for genocide, war crimes, crimes against humanity and the crime of aggression. Follow full live coverage below.

entries.title: Peacekeepers step up support as families return to south Lebanon
entries.description: With violence in south Lebanon significantly decreased since mid-June, UN peacekeepers there have returned to core functions such as protecting humanitarian aid and restoring critical infrastructure as families continue to return home.

entries.title: West Africa and the Sahel: Terrorism is changing its face
entries.description: Jihadist groups are no longer content with launching attacks in West Africa and the Sahel: they administer territories, control trade routes, exploit new technologies and are gradually pushing their influence all the way to the Gulf of Guinea.

entries.title: World News in Brief: Aid deliveries to Gaza restricted, UN prepares El Nino response, El Salvador eliminates disease
entries.description: The UN World Food Programme (WFP) is calling for greater humanitarian access to Gaza, warning that restrictions on aid deliveries, ongoing violence and funding shortages are severely limiting its ability to reach people in need.
